quantifier_attack.worker_claim: every Python-level container owner can reach is caller-reachable/re-assignable
grounded_subset: object.__setattr__ on frozen dataclass/slots when supported
quantifier_attack.why_not_required: arbitrary same-interpreter code mutation defeats Python-observable decision authenticity even without universal proof about each container

property_split.custody_secret: native opaque capsule can protect owner ledger from ordinary Python reflection under restricted native/OS attacker
property_split.decision_entrypoint: must ensure trusted native decision is actually invoked and not replaced by Python wrapper/callsite
property_split.result_acceptance: must ensure consuming verifier is independent of attacker-controlled Python; cryptographic proof only meaningful if its verifier cannot be bypassed

concrete_python_seams.bypass: hostile Python can replace callable independent of native ledger
hostile Python can replace validation flow or result

native_C.conditional_gain: opaque C owner state and native-only operation/capability check reduce state-transplant risk
native_C.fails_to_establish: arbitrary hostile same-interpreter Python cannot mint positive F7 receipt
remaining_attacks: replace Python import alias to native check
forge Python receipt downstream of a legitimate or skipped native call
native memory access if attacker tier expands to ctypes/OS
native_C.mandatory_requirement: trusted decision AND trusted result consumption must not pass through attacker-writable Python validation seams

IPC.conditional_gain: hostile Python cannot by reflection mutate custody in separate protected process
remaining_attacks: transport identity/cross-request replay if protocol underspecified
same-user OS/process compromise outside trusted isolation model
IPC.mandatory_requirement: authenticated request/response channel, request binding, replay resistance and independently trusted verifier/consumer

pure_python.sufficient_for: explicitly bounded public-data/trusted-code threat model subject to targeted hostile witnesses
pure_python.insufficient_for: unrestricted hostile same-interpreter code capable of replacing callsites/results

alternative: Keep the whole Python interpreter and application code in the TCB, constrain adversary to caller-owned data or enumerated untrusted inputs; do not call that arbitrary-code-resistant nonforgeability.
